newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended up at its second-highest closing level for 18 months on Wednesday due to a sudden spurt of buying on short-covering late in the session, traders said.
The yuan ended at 8.2966 against the U.S. dollar, up from 8.2975 on Tuesday. The highest closing price in the past 18 months was 8.2960 set on November 12, 1996.
Dealers said the sudden buying mainly came from a domestic bank which wanted to liquidate its short positions in the local unit.
The yuan closed down at an intra-day low of 7.2000 from 7.1539 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0730 from 1.0739 against the Hong Kong dollar.
The yuan opened slightly up at 8.2971 and consolidated between 8.2975 and 8.2980 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.2986 and a high of 8.2930.
Trading was more active than on Tuesday, with most done at 8.2975, traders said.
"The short-covering pushed the yuan up, but it had little impact on the weighted average price for the whole session and the yuan's movement in the short term," a dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to fall back to move around 8.2975 on Thursday.
